open_decisions.question: Does UAT run on staging or on production? Decide this FIRST — everything else in the prep branches off it.
options: Staging (`cman-budget-web-stg`) — requires removing SIT_IMPERSONATE and DEV_AUTH_EMAIL, deciding the cookie lifetime, warming the container (minReplicas 0), and confirming Entra consent on app registration 7035aa47…; still writes the same production database and still sends real unlabelled mail.

Production (`cman-budget-web-prd`) — zero config changes: no impersonation, no DEV override, two always-on replicas, a 14h cookie, everyone is themselves; matches the pilot already promised to management.
Staging first as a rehearsal for the testers, then re-run the acceptance cases on production.
open_decisions.recommendation: Production. Both environments run the identical image `72affd9` against the identical Fabric SQL database and both send real unlabelled mail, so staging buys no safety at all — it only adds three distortions (impersonated identities, a latent whole-app identity override, cold starts) that make UAT verdicts less trustworthy. Running on production deletes four prep items and matches the August commitment. Keep staging as the place to rehearse the script.

open_decisions.question: How does Solution Delivery get a UAT filler and a UAT approver, given its only filler is Suchanya and both she and Laddawan report to Arthid (101622)?
options: (a) Add `(10IT012000, pornthipp@chememan.com)` to `cc dept.xlsx` — Pornthip fills and submits, approver1 resolves to Laddawan automatically. Needs a production master edit, a ~24h sync wait, and a dated revert.
(b) Add Laddawan as the Solution Delivery filler — she becomes a second filler, but if she submits, approver1 is Arthid, who is not attending and would receive a real unlabelled approval email.
(c) Invite the real people: Suchanya as filler and Arthid as approver1. Zero master edits, fully realistic, seven attendees instead of five.

(d) Let Pornthip or Laddawan submit and have Nipaporn use the admin step-override (`POST /approval/override-step`, admin-only, position-1-only) to skip Arthid — no master edit, but Laddawan then approves nothing for that department.
(e) Drop the second department and run a single-department round like SIT did.
open_decisions.recommendation: (a), with (c) as the better answer if two more people can be in the room. Option (a) is the only one that actually delivers 'Laddawan carries 2 departments', and it is additive — the primary key is `(cost_center, filler_email)` and 153 cost centers already carry more than one filler, so Suchanya loses nothing. Two conditions: record the pre-change SharePoint version of `cc dept.xlsx` and file the revert as a dated tracker task the same day, and tell Suchanya beforehand that her department will be written to and locked during the round. Reject (b) outright — it emails a non-participant a genuine approval request.

open_decisions.question: Does UAT write the live FY2027 planning cycle, or do we open a sandbox fiscal year first?
options: FY2027 (the only open year) with a full pre-UAT snapshot of all six `budget.*` tables and a pre-written restore script, accepting that UAT numbers sit in the real budget until cleaned.

Add a sentinel year row (e.g. 2099) to the deadline master so testers type into a throwaway year — but it arrives via the daily 06:31 sync, appears in the year picker for all 114 departments, and the previous 2099 attempt returned 403 until a real row was seeded.
FY2027 but stop the chain short of the final approval so nothing reaches the terminal APPROVED state.
open_decisions.recommendation: FY2027 with a snapshot and a pre-written, pre-reviewed un-approve script. A sentinel year does not test what UAT exists to test (the real cycle, the real deadline, the real numbers) and leaks a junk year to every department. Do not choose option 3 — reaching APPROVED end-to-end is the single most important thing UAT proves, and since the app has no reopen route, the recovery script must be written and reviewed BEFORE the round, not improvised after it.

open_decisions.question: What do UAT emails look like — real and unmarked, labelled, or redirected to one mailbox?
options: Leave as-is: `NOTIFICATIONS_DRY_RUN=false`, no label, no redirect — recipients get mail indistinguishable from production, sent as `cmanpowerbi@chememan.com`.
Set `NOTIFICATIONS_ENVIRONMENT_LABEL` (red banner plus subject prefix) for the UAT window.
Set `NOTIFICATIONS_REDIRECT_ALL_TO=<one catcher mailbox>` so no non-attendee is ever mailed.
`NOTIFICATIONS_DRY_RUN=true` — kills sending entirely and makes all 16 email cases unverifiable.
open_decisions.recommendation: Leave the mail real and unlabelled IF the round is confined to attendees only — unlabelled mail is what UAT is meant to accept — but warn Arthid and Suchanya in advance, and note that the genuine FY2027 deadline reminder fires to all real fillers on 2026-09-22, so either finish before that date or brief people that both mails are real. If any case can route to a non-attendee, switch to the redirect for the window. Never option 4: 16 of the 61 SIT cases are email cases.

open_decisions.question: What goes into the UAT pack — re-run all 61 SIT cases, or a business-acceptance subset plus the new post-SIT behaviour?
options: All 61 SIT cases re-run and re-worded for the English approval UI (11 carry now-wrong Thai expectations) — thorough but heavy for five people in three to five days.

A business-acceptance subset (~30: drop Security, Data Integrity, backend-SQL-verification cases and TC-027) plus ~25 new cases covering everything shipped after 2026-08-21 — CI theme repaint, per-diem tier 3, searchable destination, seminar GL restriction, amount toasts, trip remark, other-travel GL move, English approval copy, and two-department switching.
New and changed behaviour only (~25), assuming SIT still holds for everything else.
open_decisions.recommendation: Option 2. Twelve commits shipped AFTER the last SIT case was executed and none was ever exercised; at the same time 11 SIT cases assert Thai strings the app no longer renders, and TC-057 tests a seminar GL that the 2026-08-29 restriction now hides from a Data & Analytic filler. A subset plus the new-behaviour block is the only version that both fits the window and covers the delta. Add a `Department` column — the SIT sheet has none and a two-department round needs one — and fix the three known workbook defects: the missing `Special GL Subform` row in the Summary breakdown, the promised-but-absent Defect ID column, and the hard-coded `$4:$64` ranges with `freeze_panes = I36`.
